title: Geometry (Angles & Shapes)
description: Properties of angles, triangles, quadrilaterals, and circles.

notes.heading: Angle Rules and Geometric Reasoning
notes.body:
Geometry begins with the relationships between angles. These rules let you find unknown angles without measuring.

📌 Definition
• Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$.
• Angles around a point add to $360^\circ$.
• Vertically opposite angles are equal.

🔑 Key Concept
When two straight lines cross, they create two pairs of vertically opposite angles. Adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary.

💡 Worked Example
Two lines intersect. One angle is $(3x + 10)^\circ$ and the angle vertically opposite to it is $(5x - 30)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the size of the angle.

Step 1: Set the vertically opposite angles equal
$$3x + 10 = 5x - 30$$

Step 2: Solve
$$40 = 2x$$
$$x = 20$$

Step 3: Find the angle
$$3(20) + 10 = 70^\circ$$

✅ Check: $5(20) - 30 = 70^\circ$ ✓

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Always give a reason for each step, such as "angles on a straight line" or "vertically opposite angles are equal".
• When angles involve algebra, write an equation first, then solve.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Assuming angles are equal just because they look equal. Only use a rule you can justify from the diagram.

illustration.alt: Quick reference for angle rules on lines and around points; five triangle types (equilateral, isosceles, scalene, right-angled, obtuse); circle parts including centre, radius, diameter, arc and chord; and polygon angle formulas.
illustration.caption: Geometric reasoning relies on key angle facts. Triangles sum to 180°, quadrilaterals to 360°, and any n-sided polygon interior sum is (n−2)×180°.

notes.heading: Parallel Lines and Transversals
notes.body:
When a transversal crosses parallel lines, special pairs of angles are formed. These facts are only true when the lines are parallel.

📌 Definition
• Corresponding angles are in matching positions — equal.
• Alternate angles are between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal — equal.
• Co-interior angles are between the parallel lines on the same side — add to $180^\circ$.

🔑 Key Concept
Look for the F shape (corresponding), Z shape (alternate), and C shape (co-interior) to identify the angle pairs quickly.

💡 Worked Example
Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One alternate angle is $(2x + 15)^\circ$ and the corresponding angle on the same side is $(4x - 25)^\circ$. Find $x$.

Step 1: Identify the relationship
Alternate angles are equal, so the alternate angle is also $(2x + 15)^\circ$. The corresponding angle is equal to this alternate angle because both match the same position relative to the parallel lines.

Step 2: Write the equation
$$2x + 15 = 4x - 25$$

Step 3: Solve
$$40 = 2x$$
$$x = 20$$

✅ Check: $2(20) + 15 = 55^\circ$ and $4(20) - 25 = 55^\circ$ ✓

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Parallel lines are marked with arrowheads.
• Never use corresponding/alternate angle facts unless the lines are stated to be parallel.

⚠️ Common Misconception
Confusing alternate and co-interior angles. Alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles add to $180^\circ$.

notes.heading: Triangles: Classification, Angles and Exterior Angles
notes.body:
Triangles are the simplest polygons, and their angle properties are used everywhere in geometry.

📌 Definition
A triangle is a three-sided polygon. The sum of its interior angles is always $180^\circ$.

🔑 Types of Triangles
• Equilateral: three equal sides, three equal angles of $60^\circ$.
• Isosceles: two equal sides; the angles opposite those sides are equal.
• Scalene: no equal sides and no equal angles.
• Right-angled: one angle is $90^\circ$.

🔑 Exterior Angle Property
When a side of a triangle is extended, the exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles:
$$\text{exterior angle} = a + b$$

💡 Worked Example 1
A triangle has angles $45^\circ$ and $(2x)^\circ$. The third angle is $(x + 15)^\circ$. Find $x$.

Step 1: Use the angle sum
$$45 + 2x + x + 15 = 180$$

Step 2: Simplify and solve
$$60 + 3x = 180$$
$$3x = 120$$
$$x = 40$$

Step 3: Find the angles
$2x = 80^\circ$ and $x + 15 = 55^\circ$.

✅ Check: $45^\circ + 80^\circ + 55^\circ = 180^\circ$ ✓

💡 Worked Example 2
An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of $30^\circ$. Find each base angle.

Step 1: Find the total of the two base angles
$$180^\circ - 30^\circ = 150^\circ$$

Step 2: Divide equally
$$150^\circ \div 2 = 75^\circ$$

⚠️ Common Mistake
In an isosceles triangle, the equal angles are opposite the equal sides, not next to them.

notes.heading: Quadrilaterals and Their Properties
notes.body:
Quadrilaterals are four-sided polygons. Knowing their properties helps you classify shapes and find missing angles.

📌 Definition
A quadrilateral is a polygon with four sides. The sum of its interior angles is $360^\circ$.

🔑 Key Properties
• Square: four equal sides, four right angles, opposite sides parallel, diagonals equal and bisect at $90^\circ$.
• Rectangle: opposite sides equal and parallel, four right angles, diagonals equal.
• Parallelogram: opposite sides equal and parallel, opposite angles equal, diagonals bisect each other.
• Rhombus: four equal sides, opposite sides parallel, opposite angles equal, diagonals bisect at $90^\circ$.
• Trapezium: exactly one pair of parallel sides.
• Kite: two pairs of adjacent equal sides, one pair of opposite angles equal, diagonals cross at $90^\circ$.

💡 Worked Example
A quadrilateral has angles $95^\circ$, $110^\circ$ and $(2x)^\circ$. The fourth angle is $(x + 25)^\circ$. Find $x$.

Step 1: Use the angle sum
$$95 + 110 + 2x + x + 25 = 360$$

Step 2: Simplify
$$230 + 3x = 360$$

Step 3: Solve
$$3x = 130$$
$$x = \frac{130}{3} \approx 43.3^\circ$$

Step 4: Find the angles
$2x \approx 86.7^\circ$ and $x + 25 \approx 68.3^\circ$.

✅ Check: $95 + 110 + 86.7 + 68.3 = 360$ ✓

📎 Key Points to Remember
• A square is a special rectangle, a special rhombus, and a special parallelogram.
• The hierarchy matters: if a shape has all the properties of a rectangle and a rhombus, it is a square.

⚠️ Common Misconception
Thinking a rhombus always has right angles. Only a square (a special rhombus) has right angles.

notes.heading: Circle Properties: Circumference and Area
notes.body:
Circles appear in many real-world and mathematical contexts. The two most important formulas involve the radius $r$.

📌 Definition
• Radius ($r$): distance from the centre to any point on the circle.
• Diameter ($d$): distance across the circle through the centre, $d = 2r$.
• Circumference ($C$): distance around the circle.
• Area ($A$): space inside the circle.

🔑 Key Formulas
$$C = 2\pi r = \pi d$$
$$A = \pi r^2$$

💡 Worked Example 1 — Circumference
Find the circumference of a circle with radius $7\text{ cm}$. Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$.

Step 1: Substitute into $C = 2\pi r$
$$C = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7$$

Step 2: Calculate
$$C = 44\text{ cm}$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Area
Find the area of a circle with diameter $10\text{ cm}$. Use $\pi = 3.14$.

Step 1: Find the radius
$$r = 10 \div 2 = 5\text{ cm}$$

Step 2: Substitute into $A = \pi r^2$
$$A = 3.14 \times 5^2 = 3.14 \times 25$$

Step 3: Calculate
$$A = 78.5\text{ cm}^2$$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Using the diameter directly in $A = \pi r^2$. Always halve the diameter to find the radius first.

✅ Tip
Leave answers in terms of $\pi$ unless asked for a decimal approximation. This is often more exact.

notes.heading: Perimeter and Area of Compound Shapes
notes.body:
Compound shapes are made by joining simple shapes together. To solve problems, split the shape, calculate each part, and combine the results.

📌 Definition
A compound shape is a shape made from two or more simple shapes, such as rectangles, triangles, and semicircles.

🔑 Key Concept
• For area: split the shape into simple parts, find each area, then add (or subtract cut-out parts).
• For perimeter: add only the outside edges. Missing side lengths can often be found by comparing opposite sides.

💡 Worked Example
A running track consists of a rectangle $80\text{ m}$ by $50\text{ m}$ with a semicircle on each end. The semicircles have diameter $50\text{ m}$. Find the perimeter of the track.

Step 1: Identify the straight parts
There are two straight sections of $80\text{ m}$ each.

Step 2: Identify the curved parts
Two semicircles with diameter $50\text{ m}$ make one full circle.

Step 3: Find the circumference of the full circle
$$C = \pi d = \pi \times 50 \approx 157.08\text{ m}$$

Step 4: Add the straight sections
$$\text{Perimeter} = 80 + 80 + 157.08 = 317.08\text{ m}$$

✅ Check: The two semicircles together equal one circle, so the curved distance is $\pi d$, not $2\pi d$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Counting internal lines as part of the perimeter. Only count edges on the outside boundary.

notes.heading: Congruence, Similarity and Transformations
notes.body:
Two shapes can be related by size, shape, or position. Understanding these relationships helps solve problems involving scaled diagrams and patterns.

📌 Definition
• Congruent shapes are identical in shape and size. Corresponding sides and angles are equal.
• Similar shapes have the same shape but different sizes. Corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio (scale factor).

🔑 Congruence Tests for Triangles
• SSS: three equal sides.
• SAS: two equal sides and the included angle.
• ASA: two equal angles and the included side.
• RHS: right angle, hypotenuse, and one other side equal.

🔑 Transformations
• Translation: slides a shape without turning or flipping.
• Reflection: flips a shape across a mirror line.
• Rotation: turns a shape around a fixed centre.
• Enlargement: changes the size by a scale factor from a centre point.

💡 Worked Example — Similar triangles
Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in the ratio $2:5$. The smaller triangle has base $6\text{ cm}$ and height $4\text{ cm}$. Find the base and height of the larger triangle.

Step 1: Find the scale factor
$$\text{Scale factor} = \frac{5}{2} = 2.5$$

Step 2: Multiply each dimension
$$\text{Base} = 6 \times 2.5 = 15\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Height} = 4 \times 2.5 = 10\text{ cm}$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Congruent shapes can be transformed onto each other by translation, reflection, or rotation.
• For similar shapes, area scales by the square of the scale factor; volume scales by the cube.

⚠️ Common Misconception
AAA is a similarity test, not a congruence test. Equal angles alone do not guarantee congruence because the triangles could be different sizes.

flashcards.definition: Angles opposite each other where two straight lines cross; they are always equal.
flashcards.example: If one angle is $72^\circ$, the vertically opposite angle is also $72^\circ$.

flashcards.definition: Angles in matching positions when a transversal crosses parallel lines; they are equal.
flashcards.example: In the F shape formed by parallel lines, both angles are $65^\circ$.

flashcards.definition: Angles between parallel lines on opposite sides of a transversal; they are equal.
flashcards.example: In the Z shape, both angles are $58^\circ$.

flashcards.definition: Angles between parallel lines on the same side of a transversal; they add to $180^\circ$.
flashcards.example: If one co-interior angle is $110^\circ$, the other is $70^\circ$.

flashcards.definition: The angle formed by extending one side of a triangle; it equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
flashcards.example: For interior angles $50^\circ$ and $60^\circ$, the exterior angle is $110^\circ$.

flashcards.definition: A triangle with two equal sides and two equal angles opposite those sides.
flashcards.example: If the vertex angle is $40^\circ$, each base angle is $70^\circ$.

flashcards.definition: A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel and equal; opposite angles are equal.
flashcards.example: A rectangle is a special parallelogram with four right angles.

flashcards.definition: The distance around a circle, calculated as $C = 2\pi r$ or $C = \pi d$.
The space inside a circle, calculated as $A = \pi r^2$.
Triangles that are identical in shape and size; corresponding sides and angles are equal.
flashcards.example: SSS, SAS, ASA, and RHS are tests for congruence.

flashcards.definition: Shapes with the same shape but different sizes; corresponding angles are equal and sides are in proportion.
flashcards.example: Scale factor $3$: each side triples, but area becomes $9$ times larger.

flashcards.definition: A way to move or change a shape: translation, reflection, rotation, or enlargement.
flashcards.example: Reflecting a triangle in the $y$-axis changes the sign of every $x$-coordinate.

questions.stem: Two angles sit on a straight line. One angle is $(2x + 20)^\circ$ and the other is $(3x - 10)^\circ$. Find $x$.
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$, so $(2x + 20) + (3x - 10) = 180$. This gives $5x + 10 = 180$, so $5x = 170$ and $x = 34$.

questions.stem: Three angles meet at a point: $95^\circ$, $110^\circ$ and $(3x + 5)^\circ$. Find $x$.
questions.explanation: Angles around a point add to $360^\circ$. So $95 + 110 + 3x + 5 = 360$, giving $210 + 3x = 360$, $3x = 150$, and $x = 50$.

questions.stem: Two straight lines cross. One angle is $48^\circ$. What is the size of the angle vertically opposite to it?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal. Therefore the angle opposite $48^\circ$ is also $48^\circ$.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One corresponding angle is $(4x - 10)^\circ$ and another corresponding angle is $(3x + 20)^\circ$. Find $x$.
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal, so $4x - 10 = 3x + 20$. Subtracting $3x$ gives $x - 10 = 20$, so $x = 30$.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles $55^\circ$ and $75^\circ$. What is the size of the third angle?
questions.explanation: Angles in a triangle add to $180^\circ$. The third angle is $180 - 55 - 75 = 50^\circ$.

questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of $46^\circ$. What is the size of each base angle?
questions.explanation: The two base angles are equal. Their total is $180 - 46 = 134^\circ$, so each base angle is $134 \div 2 = 67^\circ$.

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has angles $100^\circ$, $95^\circ$, $85^\circ$ and $x^\circ$. Find $x$.
questions.explanation: Angles in a quadrilateral add to $360^\circ$. So $x = 360 - 100 - 95 - 85 = 80$.

questions.stem: A triangle has interior angles $38^\circ$ and $52^\circ$. One side is extended to form an exterior angle. What is the size of that exterior angle?
questions.explanation: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: $38 + 52 = 90^\circ$.

questions.stem: Find the circumference of a circle with radius $14\text{ cm}$. Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$.
Find the area of a circle with diameter $12\text{ cm}$. Use $\pi = 3.14$.
questions.explanation: The radius is $12 \div 2 = 6\text{ cm}$. Then $A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times 36 = 113.04\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.stem: A compound shape is made from a rectangle $10\text{ cm}$ by $6\text{ cm}$ joined to a square of side $4\text{ cm}$. What is the total area?
questions.explanation: Rectangle area $= 10 \times 6 = 60\text{ cm}^2$. Square area $= 4 \times 4 = 16\text{ cm}^2$. Total area $= 60 + 16 = 76\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.stem: A triangle has area $42\text{ cm}^2$ and base $12\text{ cm}$. What is its perpendicular height?
questions.explanation: Using $A = \frac{1}{2}bh$, we have $42 = \frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times h = 6h$. Therefore $h = 42 \div 6 = 7\text{ cm}$.

questions.stem: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in the ratio $3:7$. The smaller triangle has base $9\text{ cm}$. What is the base of the larger triangle?
questions.explanation: The scale factor from small to large is $\frac{7}{3}$. So the larger base is $9 \times \frac{7}{3} = 21\text{ cm}$.

questions.stem: A rectangular field is $80\text{ m}$ long and $50\text{ m}$ wide. A path $2\text{ m}$ wide runs all the way around the inside edge. What is the area of the path?
questions.explanation: Total area $= 80 \times 50 = 4\,000\text{ m}^2$. Inner dimensions are $80 - 4 = 76\text{ m}$ and $50 - 4 = 46\text{ m}$, so inner area $= 76 \times 46 = 3\,496\text{ m}^2$. Path area $= 4\,000 - 3\,496 = 504\text{ m}^2$.

questions.stem: Which transformation maps every point $(x, y)$ to $(-x, y)$?
questions.explanation: Reflecting in the $y$-axis changes the sign of the $x$-coordinate while keeping the $y$-coordinate the same, so $(x, y) \to (-x, y)$.
